creative_intent: Weapon macro study with sword-first identity and forged metal geometry priority.

must_have: readable contour evidence of a greatsword
clear silhouette of an engineered weapon
full vertical framing of the greatsword
exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture

material.primary: forged steel / titanium / dark industrial alloy

composition.background: neutral, non-distracting background to highlight material

constraints: avoid harsh shadows that obscure form
color must remain subordinate to material identity
color must follow form then material, never override them
no flat color, always material texture variation
pure white and pure black are forbidden
charcoal black must keep temperature variation, never dead pure black
restrained crimson only in seams, cores, or controlled heat accents
muted earth support only, low saturation material support tones

core_risks: Drift into abstract forms or non-object reads
Material misinterpretation (e.g., glossy plastic, plaster, generic ceramic)
Failure to achieve dry, dense, matte finish
Object becoming secondary to texture or atmosphere
material misread as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
anti_drift_rules: Subject must remain a clearly identifiable engineered greatsword
Prevent any abstract, texture-only, or atmosphere-first interpretations
Strictly avoid generic ceramic or porcelain reads, focusing only on B4C technical ceramic
Preserve material-only scope without losing the manufactured object read
Ensure readable contour evidence of the greatsword is always present
always preserve one clearly readable manufactured object
do not let texture or atmosphere become the subject
keep material identity locked and explicit
form -> material -> color priority is mandatory
do not allow neon, pure white, pure black, or plastic-clean RGB drift
crimson may appear only as restrained seam/core accent when applicable
weapon lane wins over ceramic or mask bias
subject must read as sword first and material second
do not allow ceramic, porcelain, plastic, or rounded industrial object drift
keep blade geometry elongated, straight, and engineered
success_criteria: Immediate recognition of an engineered greatsword
Accurate and clean rendering of matte B4C technical ceramic
Material exhibits dry, dense, and engineered characteristics
No visual cues of plaster, gypsum, chalk, concrete, carved stone, mineral drift, glossy plastic, PVC sheen, or toy-like finish
Object remains the sole, clearly defined subject
image does not collapse into abstract texture or atmosphere
color feels subtractive and pigment-like, never RGB-clean
shadow mass dominates and color remains materially grounded
image reads immediately as a straight engineered greatsword
blade geometry is explicit and not abstract
material reads as forged metal, steel, titanium, or dark industrial alloy
direction_summary: Zenith Blade macro, sword-first, straight engineered greatsword, forged dark industrial alloy, no ceramic drift.
